newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB to carry out management reshuffle plan.
newsitem.headline: DKB to carry out management reshuffle plan.

text.p: Japan's Dai-ichi Kangyo Bank said on Thursday that it will carry out its management reshuffle as planned, with vice president Ichiro Fujita taking over as president and another vice president, Yoshiharu Mani, taking over as chairman in June.
"We are planning to carry through with it," Mani told reporters.
Asked whether the bank will further clarify management responsibility for its involvement in the racketeer pay-off scandal, he said that he felt that it had already done so.
The bank announced the resignations of president Katsuhiko Kondo and chairman Tadashi Okuda on May 23 to take responsibility for the revelations about the bank's links with corporate racketeers.
Fujita and Mani are to replace Kondo and Okuda, respectively, after DKB's shareholder meeting on June 27.
Earlier on Thursday, Tokyo prosecutors arrested four DKB officials on suspicion of making illegal loans to corporate racketeers.

Mani said Fujita was the most appropriate person to guide the company through its difficulties, adding that Fujita has the ability to make a fair judgement in order to promote more transparent business practises in the bank.

Asked about the speculation that Fujita had known about the illegal loans made by DKB to a brother of a racketeer in 1995 but had failed to report it to the bank president, Mani said Fujita did not report to the loan because he believed that they were ordinary unrecoverable loans.
